severity: decision
description: Recovering probe's suppressed pairs by letter-splitting costs `n + C(n,2)` clashscore invocations — ~45 min per model on the 6-conformer 7KR0 (one run is 121 s), unaffordable per candidate model on 4 CPUs. **Decision: two-tier.** (i) Every candidate model gets the cheap tier: one probe run + the network-aware post-filter, plus `autoref/clash_sweep.py`, a gemmi geometric sweep (0.4 s on 7KR0, 9 s on the 6-conformer model) that enumerates the cross-network cross-letter contacts probe structurally cannot report. (ii) The full `n + C(n,2)` recovery runs on the **final** model per target and on any model whose sweep is non-empty; both numbers are reported side by side. **Measured**: deposited 7KR0 has **30 protein-protein clashes probe cannot see** (overlaps 0.63–0.75 Å, occupancy weights to 0.36; worst is Glu A64 OE2(B) vs His A86 HE2(A), 0.754 Å at weight 0.357). 3TC7 and 3QUE have none (single/no altloc network). 7KR0-6conf has 16, all water-water at weights ≤ 0.013.

severity: **threshold change, disclosed**
description: `thresholds_v2.yaml` makes the bond/angle RMSD caps resolution-banded. v1's flat 0.020 Å bond cap made the geometry gate **degenerate at ultra-high resolution** — it would have rejected every 7KR0 candidate, which PROTOCOL §8 calls a bug. The bands come from measurement, not preference: bond RMSD recomputed on our own pipeline for every reference model we hold gives 7KR0 deposited **0.0301** and **PDB-REDO 0.0397** at 0.77 Å, against 3TC7 0.0075/0.0107 at 1.5 Å and 3QUE 0.0156/0.0104 at 2.7 Å. A cap that the state-of-the-art automated re-refinement itself fails is a mis-set constant, not a standard. New caps: ≤1.0 Å → 0.045 Å / 2.5°; above → unchanged at 0.020 Å / 2.0°. **The relative caps are untouched and still do the real work** — a candidate may never degrade geometry relative to the model it came from. Configurations tried: 2 (v1 flat, v2 banded). Evidence: `state/checks/geometry_survey.json`.

severity: scope

severity: **finding (unfavourable)**
description: **Every target's rebuild work list is empty, and re-refinement does not rescue the one real candidate.** The FASTA-vs-model classifier reproduces the expected split exactly — 7KR0 and 7KR0-6conf: 4 terminal residues each; 3TC7: Met1 plus a six-residue C-terminal His-tag, i.e. a purification tag genuinely absent from the crystal; 3QUE: terminal runs at both ends **plus one real internal gap, Asp177–Tyr182**. That gap is held at `deferred` because its N-side anchor Asp176 scores RSCC 0.6309, under the frozen 0.70 floor. Hypothesis tested: our re-refined model (R-free 0.2668 vs the deposited 0.3109) should give a better map and might lift Asp176 over the line. **It does the opposite** — measured on the re-refined seed-1 map, Asp176 falls to **0.5447**, and its neighbour Thr175 drops 0.8758 → 0.8168 while Ala184 on the far side improves 0.9543 → 0.9638. The region flanking the disordered loop degrades as the rest of the model improves, which is what a partially-disordered anchor looks like. Conclusion: the blocker is physical, not a threshold artifact, and the first change the loop should attempt on 3QUE is repairing or trimming Asp176 — **not** rebuilding the loop, which anchored on an RSCC-0.54 residue would have produced garbage. The `deferred` classification earned its place.

severity: **three bugs found by the first real run (3TC7.smoke1) + fixes**
description: The mocked tests could not see these; the smoke run did, and each has a measurement. **(a) Water removal destroyed the model**: `discrete.remove_water_change` collected residue *references*, emptied the chain and re-added them; gemmi references go stale as the vector shrinks and the "applied" model had **one atom left** (the water it was meant to delete), so `phenix.real_space_correlation` saw no model. Fixed: delete by index in place. **(b) qFit `--residue C,N` writes no `multiconformer_model2.pdb`** — only `C_N_qFit_residue.pdb` and `C_N/multiconformer_residue.pdb` (qFit git main); `tools/qfit.py::run_protein` now accepts those. **(c) Every Coot change was reverted for geometry the pipeline itself created**, from two sources: Coot's backrub rotamer moves residue i±1's peptide atoms (Cys119: Coot's own output has a 1.334 Å 119→120 bond, our residue-119-only splice left 1.286 Å), and the cut-and-splice `refine_local` refined a 5 Å buffer, then threw it away, snapping every boundary bond (Ser214→Ile215 1.327 → **1.484 Å**). Fixed: Coot windows are i−1..i+1 (rotamer) / i−1..i+2 (flip) and any atom Coot moved outside the window refuses the change on record; the local refinement is now `autoref/cctbx/local_rsr.py` — `mmtbx.refinement.real_space.individual_sites.easy` on a boolean selection with the whole model's restraints, every other atom a fixed environment (`phenix.real_space_refine` offers no fixed-atom selection; checked `--show-defaults`). `refine_local` stays for the roster canary. Runs 3TC7.smoke1 and 3QUE.run1 (cycle 11) are the evidence and are kept; production restarts as 3QUE.run2 / 3TC7.run1 with clean cycle blocks.

severity: **calibration bug + fix**
description: The selection-only refinement's built-in weight optimiser (`individual_sites.easy` → `weight.run`) judges bond/angle strain over the **whole model**, which is insensitive when three residues move, so it settled on very large map weights and bought density fit with geometry the per-change gate then rejected: 3QUE.run2 cycle 21, 12 of 17 changes failed the relative bond rule (0.002 → 0.005–0.02 Å) although the changes themselves were sane. Fix: `local_rsr.py` scans a weight grid (0.1…128) from the same start and keeps the **largest** weight whose *local* bond/angle RMSD (restraints touching the selection) stays within the gate's own budget — the pre-change model's RMSD + `geometry.bond_rmsd.rel_max` / `angle_rmsd.rel_max` — measured on the pre-change model passed as `--reference-model`. No new constant: the budget is the frozen gate. Canary on 3QUE Cys119 (window 118–120): budget bond ≤ 0.00577, chose w = 32 → 0.00347 Å (w = 64 would have given 0.00601), 7 s. Runs 3QUE.run2 killed after cycle 21 (evidence kept); production continues as 3QUE.run3 (cycles 31+) and 3TC7.run1 (cycles 11+).

severity: interpretation
description: Per-residue qFit (`--residue C,N`) writes the raw MIQP conformer occupancies, which on 3TC7.run1 cycle 11 summed to 0.66–0.78; the normalisation qFit's whole-protein pipeline applies in its segment step never runs in residue mode, and the splice's 0.05 tolerance refused all 15 candidates at apply (ledger rows kept, reason recorded). Rule now: rescale the conformers to the residue's previous group sum (what qFit itself would do), record `occ_sum_raw` and the scale on the change, refuse only when the raw sum is below 0.5 (that is not a two-conformer residue). The reciprocal refinement refines occupancies anyway once altlocs exist. Two residues (Ala120/Ala121 region) came back single-conformer from qFit despite a Ringer secondary peak — that is a real "no", not a bug, and stays reverted. Two further defects in the same function were found by 3TC7.run1 cycle 12 (Asp111: applied model still at 0.34/0.45, 'occupancy sums do not hold'): the rescaled occupancies were set on an in-memory structure while `splice_residues` re-read the qFit file from disk, and two-decimal PDB occupancies can round 0.615/0.385 to 1.01 > tolerance. Fixed: rescale per conformer at two decimals with the residual on the largest conformer, write the rescaled donor, splice from it; test with an unsplit (blank-altloc) backbone. Takes effect at each run's next cycle boundary via `scripts/resume_at_boundary.sh`.

severity: **interpretation + bug fix (altloc changes)**
description: The first qFit conformers to reach the gates (3TC7.run1 cycle 13, 20 attempted, 0 accepted) were all reverted by two rules that do not describe a residue split. (1) `phenix.real_space_correlation` keys rows by altloc, so splitting Asp111 (RSCC 0.987, blank altloc) into A/B read as *removing* a well-fitting residue (D303's removed-residue floor) plus *adding* two — the split rule now: every new conformer ≥ `altloc.conformer_rscc_min` (frozen 0.70), a pruned conformer must have been below it, and the residue's occupancy-weighted RSCC may not fall by more than the frozen `rscc_min_delta` (0.01); the survivor of a collapse to one conformer is renamed, not pruned. No new constant; recorded as `rscc_gate = split_residue` on the row. (2) The clash gate identified atom pairs by name+altloc, so every pre-existing bonded-neighbour contact (C(i−1)–CA(i) 2.4 Å, O(i−1)–N(i) 2.25 Å …) reappeared as "new" once the residue's atoms carried letters — 8 to 20 phantom clashes per conformer; pairs are now identified without the altloc for atoms of the changed residues, so only genuinely new contacts count. Both measured on 3TC7.run1 c013 change_result.json files. Also measured: at 2.7 Å qFit returns a single conformer for 10 of 10 3QUE residues tried so far — a real "no", left as reverted.

severity: **rule made asymmetric**
description: 3TC7.run1 cycles 12–13: 26 waters kept "within noise" while R-free-select moved −0.00285 then **+0.00281** and the reported half worsened 0.1792 → 0.1814 → 0.1825; the signed drift guard (D402) netted the two to −0.00004 and never fired, and at 1.5 Å the solvent proposer supplies 20 RSCC-passing sites per cycle indefinitely. description: 3TC7.run2 cycle 21 (`--stages protein_altloc --max-per-stage 60`): of 60 Ringer-ranked residues, qFit returned two or more conformers for 36; 20 splits passed the local gates, 13 were reverted (new altloc-aware clashes or a conformer below 0.70), 3 prune attempts reverted. Reading: single conformers moved nothing (D412); twenty together move R-free by ~0.003 on every measure — the published qFit gain is at least partly collective, and this loop's per-cycle bar is set so that one such batch does not clear it. severity: **finding + gate fix: refinement zeroes many qFit conformers; prunes were blocked**
description: After 3TC7.run2 cycle 21's paired refinement (occupancies refined, as SPEC §6.1 requires once altlocs exist), 11 of the 20 kept conformers refined to occupancy **below the frozen 0.10 floor — most to 0.000** (Asp111 A, 137 B, 155 A, 194 A, 201 A, …; 130 B at 0.029). The data does not support those conformers; the prune proposer correctly proposed removing every one in cycle 22, and the split-residue rule (D410) refused every one because "the pruned conformer fit its density at 0.98–0.99". RSCC is occupancy-insensitive: an atom group at occupancy 0.0 contributes nothing to the map and still correlates with the density it sits in. Fix: for `protein_altloc_prune` / `ligand_altloc_prune` the pruned conformer's RSCC is not a criterion — the frozen occupancy floor is (recorded on the change as `occ_by_letter`); the residue-level no-worsening rule still applies (`rscc_gate = prune_by_occupancy`). Scientific reading, unfavourable for the qFit hypothesis: roughly half of qFit's per-residue conformers on this 1.5 Å model do not survive one round of occupancy refinement, so the −0.0031 collective gain of cycle 21 came from the other half (plus whatever the zeroed atoms contributed through B-factor/occupancy freedom).

severity: **noise source found + fix: TLS re-partitioning between cycles**
description: On 3QUE.run3 successive re-refinements of essentially the same model swung R-free-select by ±0.005 (c031 treatment 0.2529 → c032 null 0.2592 → c033 null 0.2540 → c034 0.2551 → c035 null 0.2607), several times the seed noise floor (0.00144), while 3TC7 (anisotropic B, no TLS) drifted smoothly. `phenix.find_tls_groups` is run on every refinement's input and produced a different four-group partition at cycle 34 (`resid 5–8 / 88–12x / 124–20x / 202–35x` vs `5–12x / 124–20x / 202–26x / 262–35x` before), exactly where the base jumped. Within each paired cycle both arms received the same partition (same input model), so the paired verdicts stand; the noise floor was measured from one input model and therefore never saw this. Fix: the driver pins the partition named by the run's base `refine_decisions.json` and passes it (`RefineParams.tls_selections`) to every later refinement of the run (`refine_extra`), logged in DECISIONS.md; and the run summary now reports the **best** base of the run (lowest R-free-select, with cycle and model) beside the last, because the last is no longer guaranteed best. Takes effect on 3QUE.run3 at its next boundary (partition 4827b4 from cycle 35); no effect on 3TC7 (no TLS).

severity: **three bugs from the day's experiments, all fixed**

severity: **result + rule: C3 regressed because the per-conformer prune removed residue MAJORS; a residue's major conformer is never pruned**
description: C3 (`runs/3TC7/experiments/qfit_whole/c3/`, cycle 34): C2's pruned model pruned again with C2's refined evidence (53 conformers at 42 residues: 22 clash, 19 water-density, 12 occupancy floor) → 242 conformers at 94 residues; paired from unrefined coordinates with the same weight criteria. **Regressed**: attributable **+0.0044** (2.5σ worse), R-free full 0.1841 → 0.1903, R-work 0.1473 → 0.1506, `model_vs_data` +0.0062; bond RMSD 0.019 / angle 1.75° (over the caps), MolProbity score 1.51, C-beta deviations 6, altloc-aware clashscore 4.67 (under the 5.0 cap but +2.3 over the relative cap), 72/76 split residues pass. Both pruned files are structurally sound (uniform atom counts per letter, every group sums to 1.0) and the arms are converged (last-macro-cycle ΔR-free ≤ 0.001: C 0.3316→0.1761, C2 0.3411→0.1808, C3 0.3452→0.1903), so the loss is in what was pruned. **Cause**: the clash rule ("prune the lower-occupancy lettered atom; a lettered atom clashing with a blank-altloc atom is pruned regardless") and the water rule ("any lettered conformer within 3 Å of a flagged water") can remove a residue's **major** conformer — the one the base model already had — after which `prune_conformers` rescales the surviving minor to full occupancy. Counted from `prune_list.json` against the refined occupancies: C2 pruned 30 majors of 157 letters (e.g. A38 B 0.51, A76 D 0.62), C3 15 of 60 (A71 B at **1.0**, A44 C 0.71). A major's clash or water contact is not this change's doing and pruning it is not a gate rule; it was my implementation error. **Rule** (now in `exp_qfit_whole_c2.py`): the highest-occupancy conformer of a residue is never pruned; offenders among minors are. C4 (cycle 35) re-applies C2's evidence with this rule to the *refined* C2 candidate (so both arms start converged). C2's own −0.0033 was measured with 30 majors wrongly pruned and is therefore a lower bound on the gate-clean subset's gain.

section: PROTOCOL §3.1–3.3 (flags inherited unchanged), §12 (say what you verified)
severity: **finding: the published 3TC7 R-free 0.163 is on a DIFFERENT flag set — the campaign's headline gap was never like-for-like**
description: The published qFit coordinates were fetched in-session (`https://files.dynamicpdb.com/a937eeb3-1dfd-43a3-af1a-08675aad9807/models/036b3d5e-c7e6-4f0e-ae39-37e76b3a7618/artifacts/2e719a59-01fd-4bd3-8ada-5bfdfc149940/3tc7_qFit_010.cif`, sha256 `4dbee327…62a74`, 8454 atoms, 181 residues with altlocs, 427 conformers, 328 waters) and scored with the campaign's evaluator on the frozen data and flags (`scripts/experiments/exp_score_published.py`, `runs/3TC7/experiments/published_model/`). **Their own file header**: 41052 reflections, R-free set **1993** (4.85 %), R-work 0.1382, R-free 0.1633, sigma_F 1.33. **Our flags**, inherited unchanged from the deposited structure factors: **2075** free (5.05 %). severity: **result (E017, C10): the §4.1 water audit clears every flagged water by the frozen rules, per-residue qFit builds nothing at GLN27/GLU245; the batch stays blocked on clashes (9.8) and two boundary residues**

Paired: attributable **−0.005024** (2.8σ), R-free full 0.1841 → 0.1803, report 0.1800 → 0.1775, R-work 0.1441; geometry bond 0.014 / angle 1.361 ok; split-residue rule **75/75**; audited waters all ≥ floor in the candidate (0 failures). **Clashes 9.80** (cap 5.0) — unchanged from C9, as expected for the same conformers. Density under v3 with the audit: **4** neighbour failures — GLN A27 (0.935 → 0.852), GLU A245 (0.963 → 0.884), water A739 (0.971 → 0.930, newly flagged), ligand ACY A401 (0.924 → 0.903). Ledger `3TC7.c042.protein_altloc_add.qfit_whole_pruned_c10` = `rejected`. What this settles: the water failures of the C-series were the mask effect of D442, not displacement — the frozen retention rules, applied as §4.1 orders, keep every one; the two protein residuals are not missing conformers of their own (qFit finds none) but boundary effects of their neighbours' splits — GLU245 is the single residue bonded to segment 243–244's letters, GLN27 the H-bond partner of ASP162's C/D. The fixes are structural: extend segment 243–244 through 245 (245 takes 244's letters and occupancies) and either couple GLN27 to ASP162's letters or prune the ASP162 minor it responds to. Both wait for E018 (segment-constrained occupancies), whose refined letter occupancies decide the C12 prune.

severity: **bug found (E018): qFit's `create_restraints_file.py` writes one constrained_group per LETTER — a letter is equalised along its segment but the letters no longer sum to 1; E018's refined candidate is over-occupied at 64 residues and its −0.0046 is void**
description: E018 (`runs/3TC7/experiments/qfit_whole/e018/`, cycle 43): C9's refined candidate re-refined with `qFit_occupancy.params` (76 blocks) on the candidate arm. Paired attributable **−0.004589** (2.5σ) — but `assert_occupancy_sums` on the refined candidate: **78 violations (64 groups > 1.0, up to 1.14; 14 < 1.0)**; the null arm has 0. The params file (head: `constrained_group { selection = altid A and ((chain A and resseq 5)) }`, then a separate block for altid B) defines each letter as its own group; phenix's `constrained_group` couples the selections *within* a group to sum to 1, so single-selection groups couple nothing, and the explicit groups displace phenix's automatic per-residue altloc constraint — sums float. The refined letter occupancies are therefore not occupancies (A5 0.61 + 0.42, A109 0.30 + 0.84) and neither the R-free gain nor the C12 kill list derived from them (A95 A, A111 A, A122 B, A229 C, A237 B at ≈ 0) can be used as they stand. Ledger `3TC7.c043.protein_altloc_add.qfit_whole_c9_segment_constrained` = `rejected` (bug). Fix: `autoref/stages/segment_constraints.py` — one constrained_group per backbone segment with one selection per letter (`chain A and resseq 41:54 and altloc A`, …), the coupling phenix documents; 3 unit tests. The same module adds `extend_segment_letters` (PROTOCOL §5.2: an unsplit residue bonded to a split one joins the segment). C12 (E020) is E018 redone with both. Note for SPEC §10.2 / the qFit protocol: qFit's own final-refinement script relies on this file; whether qFit's pipeline is affected the same way is worth a check before its numbers are quoted (PROTOCOL §13).

severity: **E011 void as run: the 7KR0 whole-protein qFit candidate lost the base's 1990 riding hydrogens, so its paired cycle measured hydrogens, not conformers; two gate findings for 7KR0**
description: E011 (`runs/7KR0/experiments/qfit_whole/`, cycle 6): `qfit_protein` on the campaign model (run2 cycle-3 null arm) → 98 split residues / 276 conformers (the deposited 7KR0 already carries 89 split residues; qFit re-sampled them all and split 16 more). Paired: attributable **+0.012555** (31σ), R-work +0.0127, R-free full 0.1136 → 0.1273 — but the null arm refined 4298 atoms of which **1990 hydrogens**, the candidate **2999 atoms and 0 hydrogens**: qFit writes heavy atoms only and the judge refined it as such (`find_and_add_hydrogens=False`). At 0.77 Å hydrogens carry ~1 % of R, so the comparison is void; nothing about qFit's conformers is learned. (3TC7 is unaffected: its deposited model and campaign base have no hydrogens, so every C-series arm was H-free on both sides.) Fix: `exp_qfit_whole_judge.py … add_hydrogens` sets `main.find_and_add_hydrogens=True` on the candidate arm; rerun as E011b (cycle 7, `qfit_whole/with_h/`). Two things E011 did establish: (1) the **7KR0 base's altloc-aware clashscore is 9.46**, already above the 5.0 absolute cap for d < 1.5 Å — the deposited multiconformer model violates the cap by construction, so on this target only the relative cap (+1.0) can govern a change; (2) the batch gate judges only residues *newly* split — the 89 residues qFit re-sampled (new conformers, same letters) receive no density check; a `rebuilt` class (per-letter coordinates changed beyond tolerance) should be judged by the split-residue rule. Ledger `7KR0.c006.protein_altloc_add.qfit_whole_protein` = `rejected` (void).

severity: **result (E020, C12): with coupled segment occupancies the 3TC7 qFit batch's gain halves to −0.0028 (1.6σ, uncredited) — half of the C-series' −0.005 was per-residue occupancy freedom, not conformers**
description: C12 (`runs/3TC7/experiments/qfit_whole/c12/`, cycle 44, `exp_qfit_whole_c12.py`): C9's refined candidate (86 split residues / 214 conformers; the planned GLU245 extension was skipped because C9's kills had already made 241–246 single) refined on the candidate arm with `segment_constraints.py`'s file — **34 constrained_group blocks, one per backbone segment, one selection per letter** — same base, seed and weight budget as C2–C10. Occupancies after refinement are coherent: constant along every segment, sums 1.00 (4 minor under-occupancy violations from letters that refined to ≤ 0.08: A95 A 0.06, A111 A 0.03, A122 B 0.08, A237 B 0.00); 41–54 settles at A 0.31 / B 0.44 / C 0.12 / D 0.14, 65–71 at A 0.45 / B 0.36 / C 0.20. Paired: attributable **−0.002841** (1.6σ; bar −0.00362) → `no_change`; R-free full 0.1841 → 0.1810, report 0.1800 → 0.1767, `model_vs_data` agrees in sign. Legs: split residues 75/75, geometry bond 0.016 (at the cap) / angle 1.46 ok, **clashes 11.0** (cap 5.0; the occupancy-weighted count rises because letters that had refined to ~0 at the clash sites now carry the segment's occupancy), neighbour failures 25 (v2) / 7 (v3: 4 waters + GLN27, GLU245, LYS224). Ledger `3TC7.c044.protein_altloc_add.qfit_whole_c9_segments_coupled` = `rejected`. **Reading, across the series:** the same conformers give −0.0050 to −0.0061 with per-residue occupancies (C5, C7–C10) and −0.0028 with segment-coherent ones (C12); the difference is what free per-residue backbone-letter occupancies buy, and a backbone conformer that is 58 % present at one residue and absent at the next is not a conformer (D445). Under the rules the coherent model is the only one that can be depositable, and its gain is below the noise bar. The 3TC7 whole-protein qFit batch is therefore at its floor: a real but uncreditable ≈ −0.003, with the clash and two-residue density residuals still to be paid for. Options left with a mechanistic case: sub-segment coupling groups derived from the unconstrained occupancy profiles (which residues actually co-vary), or accepting the per-residue model as a documented, non-depositable R-free result — neither is started without the operator.

severity: **rule added as a monitor (no verdict changed): the paired, noise-scaled R-gap monitor — Jaime Fraser's review point that small R-free gains need the R-free − R-work gap watched for overfitting**
description: The v1 rule (`refine.r_gap_widening_warn` 0.010, base → candidate) never fired on a credited cycle and is coarser than any gain the campaign has credited (0.003–0.008), and it mixes re-refinement into the comparison. The v4 rule compares the candidate arm with the NULL arm of the same cycle: Δgap = gap(candidate) − gap(null), judged against σ_gap = sd of (R-free_full − R-work) over the ten noise-floor seeds — measured 3TC7 0.00226, 3QUE 0.00365, 7KR0 0.00020 (gap means 0.0387, 0.0519, 0.0081). A cycle whose R-free-select improved while Δgap > k·σ_gap (k = 2) is flagged `overfit_suspect`. Implemented in `autoref/rgap.py` (pure, unit-tested) and `stages/paired.py`; new `cycles` columns `r_gap_null`, `delta_r_gap`, `gap_flag`; the GAP-<target>-c<N> deviations row now carries the paired verdict; `autoref status` prints the standing model's gap against the re-refined baseline's gap ± σ and the number of flagged cycles. `mode: gate` is implemented (credit withheld, candidate not adopted) and switched off in v4. Retro-applied to all 51 paired cycles on record (`scripts/experiments/exp_rgap_retro.py`, `runs/verify_20260907/rgap_retro.json`): flagged 3TC7 c12 (kept within noise, 13 waters, Δgap +0.0063 = 2.8σ), 7KR0 c19 (+0.0025 = 12.5σ) and c21 (+0.0040 = 20.5σ; both boltz multicopy experiments judged against a stripped null, never adopted). Credited cycles in the deliverable chains: 3TC7 c11 Δgap +0.0044 (1.9σ, 13 waters — just under the bar), 3QUE c31 −0.0059 and c41 −0.0056 (gap narrowed), 7KR0 none credited. Reading: the 3TC7 water-addition cycles are the campaign's overfit-risk zone, and the 7KR0 multicopy models widened the gap by 12–20σ while improving R-free-select — exactly the pattern the monitor exists to catch. Configurations tried before freezing (thresholds_v4 header): the v1 absolute rule; k·σ on base → candidate (fires on re-refinement alone); k·σ on candidate → null (adopted).

section: PROTOCOL §4.3 (acceptance), §3.6 / SPEC_LOOP_V2 §1.3 / SPEC_DPDB_RUNS §2 (verdict, drift guard, promotion)
severity: **rule change by version: `thresholds_v8.yaml` = v7 + `paired.metropolis` (enabled, T = 1.0·σ_select, band (0, +k·σ]) — a `no_change` paired cycle whose attributable ΔR-free-select is worse but within +k·σ keeps its treatment arm with probability exp(−Δ/T) from a recorded deterministic draw; promotion additionally requires the credited best base not to be worse than the standing record on R-free-select; `scripts/run_dpdb.sh` defaults to v8**
description: Origin: Marcus Collins's review of the 2026-09-16 write-up ("rejecting negative results is a tricky business, statistically speaking … some amount of Monte Carlo/Metropolis") and Spencer's question whether a specific test decides when a credited model replaces the current one. Reading of the harness as it stood (v1–v7): `paired.decide_verdict` credits ≤ −k·σ, bisects > +k·σ, and in between D411 keeps the treatment arm iff attributable ≤ 0 — a hard boundary at zero inside a band whose width is the measured noise of exactly that comparison, so +0.5σ and −0.5σ are the same evidence and the rule prefers the changes that were lucky on the consulted half; greedy descent on a noisy objective stops at the first plateau. Change: `autoref/metropolis.py` (pure, tested) — p_keep = exp(−Δ/(temperature_sigma·σ_select)), u = sha256(target, cycle_index, seed) → [0,1), keep iff u < p; applied in `paired.run_paired_cycle` only when the frozen thresholds carry `paired.metropolis.enabled`, only for `no_change` with 0 < attributable ≤ k·σ, never when a gate (R-gap, divergence) has refused the candidate. Unchanged: the credit bar, the regression bar and its bisection, the R-gap gate (D495), the divergence gate (D497), the geometry/clash/RSCC gates, D484 (promotion on credit only). Bound: the SPEC_DPDB_RUNS §2 drift guard (cumulative un-credited drift > +k·σ → every kept change row `rejected`, base ← last credited base) is now armed after every Metropolis keep as well; the last-credited pointer is the run's start base until the first credit, so the walk can never end below the start model (a missing pointer falls back to the run's best base by R-free-select; `_track_best` now runs at cycle 0). Record: the decision (p, u, T, kept) is in `paired_cycle.json`, `cycle.json["metropolis"]` and DECISIONS.md. Promotion (Spencer's question, the test that exists): `_promote` moves `state/current/<T>.json` only when (a) the run credited something (D484), (b) NEW: the run's best base is not worse than the standing record on R-free-select (a tie from a different model is refused; re-writing the same model is not a replacement) — a credit is relative to the run's own null arm, not to the deliverable — else a `PROMOTE-<T>-c<N>` deviations row, and (c) the deliverable's R-gap does not widen beyond 2σ_gap (D495). Of the 13 credits on record, 7 moved a deliverable (3QUE c031, c041; 3TC7 c011, c057; 7KR0 c033, c035, c037); the 6 that did not: 3TC7 c058 (E029, beat its H-free null, worse than c057 on report/full), 3TC7 c064 and c068 (deliverable gap bound, D495/D498), 7KR0 c017/c019/c021 (sampleworks distillation credited against their own null arms at 0.226/0.124/0.126 full, above the 0.113 deliverable; never promoted because experiments do not promote). Retro-judgement (`state/exports/cycles.csv`, today's noise-floor rows σ_select 3QUE 0.00144 / 3TC7 0.000084 / 7KR0 0.000405, seed 1): of 84 paired cycles, 17 were `no_change` with 0 < attributable ≤ 2σ (3QUE 8, 3TC7 3, 7KR0 6); Metropolis at T = 1σ would have kept 9 of them (3QUE c033 +0.05σ, c036 +0.11σ, c038 +0.34σ; 3TC7 c031 +0.49σ, c053 +0.40σ; 7KR0 c003 +0.95σ, c032 +0.60σ, c040 +0.01σ, c041 +0.18σ) and dropped 8 (all four 3QUE cycles at +1.8σ, 3QUE c083, 3TC7 c025, 7KR0 c001, c042); no credit, no promotion and no deliverable would have changed, because those follow from the credit bar alone. Tests: `tests/test_metropolis.py` (6), `tests/test_run_discrete.py::test_metropolis_keep_is_uncredited_and_bounded_by_the_drift_guard`, `::test_promotion_refused_when_credited_base_is_not_below_the_standing_record`. Configurations tried: 1 (T = 1.0σ; the unit the campaign already measures, no new constant). Applies to the phase-2 targets (D501) from their first cycle; 3TC7/3QUE/7KR0 are unchanged until re-run.

Every `targets/targets.yaml` value is the literal output of `https://data.rcsb.org/rest/v1/core/entry/<ID>` executed 2026-09-16 (saved with the run): all X-ray, 1.00–1.70 Å, structure factors released (`status_code_sf` REL); depositor R-work/R-free from `refine[0]`; free-set sizes 528 (4QO4, PROTOCOL §3.7 small-set note; header carries no cross-validation method) to 3587 (3DUT); 9D5Y/9D5U carry a 2 % free set; deposited refinement programs PHENIX (4), REFMAC (4), CNS (4), X-PLOR (1) — the CNS/X-PLOR entries' flag conventions are decided by `autoref/flags.py` from `_refln.status` / `pdbx_r_free_flag` at prep, and a file with no flag column halts that target (PROTOCOL §3.1) rather than generating one. Method: `scripts/onboard_target.sh` (fetch → prep → dossier → verify → noise-floor n=10 → baseline) then `scripts/run_dpdb.sh <T> --max-cycles 8` (correction, solvent, protein_altloc, adp_model ladder of SPEC_DPDB_RUNS §3; paired null control; site-restricted reciprocal step; R-gap, divergence and Metropolis rules of v8), orchestrated by `scripts/run_phase2.sh` (13 in parallel, `AUTOREF_NPROC` 24). No per-target `--refine-extra`: the standing 3QUE/3TC7 overrides are target-specific findings (D421, D496). Hydrogens: the deposited models are refined as deposited (mostly without riding H); PROTOCOL §4.1 as amended on main now permits riding H below 2.0 Å for all thirteen, and 3TC7's −0.011 credit (D488) says it can matter — H is a per-target paired experiment after the base runs (E028 pattern), not part of onboarding, because the ADP-weight optimiser's behaviour on H-bearing models needed a per-target fix (D491, D496). Disclosure: main's PROTOCOL §4.7 (L1–L10 with qFit at L3/L4, a standing `phenix.refine` block with `ordered_solvent=True` every macro-cycle and variants A/B, `solvent_model_select`, `zone_shift`, `backbone_split`) and §4.1 (four cooperating agents) describe a method the harness does not implement; the phase-2 runs follow SPEC_DPDB_RUNS as reviewed on 2026-09-08 (D480/D481). Whether to build the ladder is an operator decision; this row records that the two documents now disagree and which one the runs followed.
